title: OET and Medical English — registration with the GMC, NMC and DHA
meta_description: Preparation for doctors, nurses, dentists and pharmacists sitting OET or the IELTS 7.0-each requirement, delivered with Future MedsAcademy.

props.heading: Doctors and nurses need a different English exam.
props.intro: The Occupational English Test is the healthcare-specific alternative to IELTS, accepted by the GMC, NMC, AHPRA, the Medical Council of Ireland and dozens of other regulators. Every task is set in a clinical context — and that is exactly why it suits medics and why generic preparation fails.
rows: Clinical — patient notes, referral letters, consultations
A referral or discharge letter from case notes
A report and an argumentative essay
Two clinical role-plays with a patient
props.footnote: Our advice: if your only goal is to practise, take OET — the vocabulary is already yours. If you also plan to study, take IELTS Academic, which covers both.

side.title: The four OET sub-tests

items.title: Listening · 45 min, all professions
items.body: Patient consultations and a workplace presentation. Note-taking under clinical pressure.

items.title: Reading · 60 min, all professions
items.body: Guidelines, package inserts, policy documents and journal extracts. Part A is fifteen minutes of pure speed.

items.title: Writing · 45 min, profession-specific
items.body: One letter — usually a referral — written from real case notes. Selecting the relevant clinical detail is the whole skill.

items.title: Speaking · 20 min, profession-specific
items.body: Two role-plays with an interlocutor playing your patient. Graded on clinical communication as well as language.

side.note: Twelve professions: medicine, nursing, dentistry, pharmacy, physiotherapy, occupational therapy, radiography, optometry, podiatry, speech pathology, veterinary science and dietetics.

props.eyebrow: How Bloom and FMA deliver it together
props.heading: Language teachers and practising clinicians, in the same course.
props.body: OET fails candidates who have excellent clinical English and no idea what an examiner wants from a referral letter — and candidates whose English is fine but whose role-play manner is not. We put both specialists in the room.

cards.title: Role-plays with real medics
cards.body: Future MedsAcademy clinicians play your patient, so the scenario behaves like a consultation rather than a language exercise.

cards.title: Referral letters marked twice
cards.body: Once by a language examiner for the four criteria, once by a clinician for whether the letter would actually be useful to the receiving doctor.

cards.title: Registration pathway included
cards.body: GMC and NMC applications, PLAB and CBT preparation, and Italian and EU medical routes through Future MedsAcademy.

cards.title: One account across both academies
cards.body: Your Bloom profile and your FMA study record sit side by side — English on one side, clinical preparation on the other.

side.heading: What each regulator asks for
side.footnote: Requirements change. We confirm the current rule with the regulator before you book a test — and tell you if a single-skill retake would be cheaper than a full sitting.
